gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-hk: Retro and loud, Styro squeezes its letters together until every bowl nearly seals shut. But Noto Sans HK, a plain sans, lifts its brush ends early and leaves every curve open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Styro crowds its letters into a tight, retro block, bowls nearly sealed shut and gaps all but gone. Closed against open: Noto Sans Kaithi, a sans, supplies all the openness.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Retro Styro crowds its letters, bowls nearly sealed. Noto Sans Kharoshthi, a sans-serif with unclosed curves, lays a dark stripe down every line, so a full column feels friendly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Retro and crowded, Styro squeezes its letters together until every gap nearly vanishes. Noto Sans Khmer, a sans with chisel-notch openings and tall small letters, makes that closed-against-open contrast the whole point.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Modern Noto Sans Khojki gives every e a large, clear eye. Beside Styro, whose retro letters crowd almost shut, that open sans makes the pair's whole appeal: tight set against light.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Letters pressed almost into each other give Styro its retro, commanding push. Noto Sans Khudawadi, a sans-serif with unlatched rounds and modest capital height, gives that push room to breathe on the page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-lao: Styro crowds its retro letters together until the bowls barely leave a gap. Noto Sans Lao, a sans whose lifted x-height keeps the mouths open, loosens everything up again.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Retro and tightly packed, Styro leaves almost no daylight inside its letters. Noto Sans Medefaidrin, a sans-serif whose lowercase rises high without ink pooling, should read smoothly down a whole page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Styro is retro and commanding, its letters jammed close with barely a gap in the bowls. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek, a sans with cracked-bangle rounds and large eyes, should read easily line after line.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Crowded letters, jammed so close that the bowls nearly seal, give Styro its retro, commanding grip on a line. Styro commands, while Noto Sans Meroitic, a sans, stays see-through.
